question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Metals and Non-metals Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Which metal can be easily cut with a butter knife due to its low density and softness?
options: Iron
Sodium
Aluminium
Copper
questions.correct_answer: Sodium

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes key observations in Metals and Non-metals (Set 1)?
options: Core process in Metals and Non-metals obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.
Process in Metals and Non-metals violates mass conservation.
No physical or chemical state change occurs during the reaction.
Products have higher total mass than initial reactants.
questions.correct_answer: Core process in Metals and Non-metals obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.

questions.question_text: What physical state symbol or indicator color change is associated with Metals and Non-metals (Set 1)?
options: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change
Solid precipitate (s) with gas emission
Gaseous phase (g) only
Liquid phase (l) with zero temperature change
questions.correct_answer: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change

questions.question_text: Identify the correct SI unit or mathematical relationship relevant to Metals and Non-metals (Set 1).
options: Standard NCERT Formula & Unit
Dimensionless Ratio x 100
Inverse Square Exponential
Absolute Constant Zero
questions.correct_answer: Standard NCERT Formula & Unit

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Fundamental processes in Metals and Non-metals strictly follow thermodynamic and chemical principles.
Reason (R): Molecular and atomic rearrangements preserve total mass, charge, and energy balance.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Metals and Non-metals Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Differentiate between Roasting and Calcination in metallurgy.
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Roasting heats sulphide ores in excess air to convert them into oxides; Calcination heats carbonate ores in limited/absent air to convert them into oxides.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Metals and Non-metals Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Explain the Thermit reaction and state its major practical application.
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Thermit reaction is the highly exothermic reduction of Iron(III) oxide by Aluminium powder: Fe2O3(s) + 2Al(s) -> 2Fe(l) + Al2O3(s) + Heat. The molten iron produced is used to weld broken railway tracks.
